self_critique:
What was suboptimal

- The run converged too early after only five nodes. Two rejected local ideas and one small ensemble gain are not enough evidence that the search space is exhausted.
- Node_001 used a broad factorial sweep and selected the winner on the same validation signal used for reporting. The +0.0025 gain may include multiple-comparison/selection bias, but no confirmation split or fresh-seed replication was reported.
- The policy repeatedly asserted “early validation peak followed by decline” despite the journal noting that the parent curve was missing. Diagnosis should have been grounded in stored curves, checkpoint metrics, and train–validation gaps rather than inherited narrative.
- Uncertainty handling was weak. The final gain from 0.6043 to 0.6049 is only about 0.0006, yet there are no paired-seed results, confidence intervals, or ensemble-member covariance estimates. The baseline sigma alone is insufficient.
- Node_004 bundled member count, averaging method, seed diversity, and LR jitter. Acceptance identifies an ensemble recipe, but not which component produced the gain or whether the gain is simply variance reduction from extra compute.
- Rejected nodes changed several feature/weighting elements at once. This made failures hard to interpret and consumed trials without producing clean causal information.
- Compute-normalized comparisons were absent. A 5–7 member ensemble should be compared against equally expensive alternatives or at least reported with its inference/training cost.

What I would change in the scaffold

- Require every proposal to cite concrete diagnostics: best epoch, post-peak degradation, seed variance, subgroup metrics, and calibration/ranking decomposition.
- Separate exploration from confirmation: use one validation slice for selection and a locked temporal confirmation slice or nested resampling for final acceptance.
- Require paired seeds and report mean delta, standard error, and worst-seed delta for improvements below roughly 0.001.
- Decompose compound sweeps. After a winning factorial configuration, run minimal ablations against the parent before launching another broad search.
- Track selection count and adjust confidence thresholds for repeated validation queries.
- Store full learning curves and checkpoint decisions so later nodes do not rely on unsupported summaries.
- Include compute and latency in the objective or, at minimum, in the acceptance record.
- Avoid declaring convergence until the current champion has been independently reproduced and at least one orthogonal model or data intervention has been tested cleanly.

What the next run should try first

First, independently confirm node_004 on fresh seeds and a locked temporal holdout. Compare:

1. Single best DCN-lite model.
2. Three-member seed ensemble.
3. Five-member seed ensemble.
4. Probability averaging versus per-user-rank averaging.
5. Seed-only diversity versus LR-jitter diversity.

Use identical checkpoints where possible and report paired deltas, variance, and cost. This will determine whether 0.604927 is a robust improvement or validation-selected noise.

If confirmed, retain the smallest ensemble that captures nearly all of the gain. Then ablate the node_001 champion one factor at a time—architecture, loss, recency weighting, and regularization—to establish which interactions are real. Only after that should the run revisit new features or recency schemes, preferably as isolated changes with fresh-seed confirmation.
